scope: Labels attached to user-channel decision points in two-channel (user + assistant) clips. A label is a statement about what a correct system SHOULD do at the stated point; it is never a model output.

complete.definition: The user has finished a contribution and released the floor; a response is due.
complete.system_should: take the floor (respond) after the user's last speech frame; an end-of-turn decision is allowed from user_speech_end_s onwards and its delay is the signed latency.

gold.eot_gold_s: time of the last user speech sample (end of the final word; fade excluded)

complete.scoring_role: positive for end-of-turn recall and signed latency; an end-of-turn decision BEFORE eot_gold_s is a cut-in, scored as an early (negative-latency) event, not as a hit.

incomplete.definition: The user is mid-turn: the clause is syntactically or semantically unfinished at the pause (function-word cut, hesitation, restart in progress), so more speech is expected.
incomplete.system_should: hold; neither respond nor stop its own output because of this pause.

gold.hold_window_s: [user_speech_end_s, clip_end_s] - digital silence of exactly 2.0 s on both channels

incomplete.scoring_role: negative for false cuts: any end-of-turn event inside hold_window_s counts once as a false cut (EOT FPR / mid-turn-pause FPR).

backchannel.definition: A short acknowledgement ('yeah', 'okay', 'mm hm', 'I see') produced while the OTHER party holds the floor; it is not a bid for the floor.
backchannel.system_should: keep the floor (keep speaking); do not stop output, do not treat the acknowledgement as an end of the user's turn.
backchannel.scoring_role: negative for interruption false positives (INT FPR) and for policy yield/keep (a stop or an end-of-turn here is a false yield).

wait.definition: The user explicitly asks the system to hold ('hold on', 'give me a second', 'one moment') and has not yet given the content; the floor stays reserved for the user although the user is silent.
wait.system_should: not respond and not time out into a response during the hold window; a short non-committal acknowledgement is permitted only if the policy under test declares it.
wait.scoring_role: negative for false cuts (same arithmetic as incomplete); reported as its own stratum because a silence-timer baseline and a semantic arm can differ here.

turn_state_notes: The four states are mutually exclusive per decision point. 'complete' is the only state with an end-of-turn positive.
A decision point is the user_speech_end_s of a clip (clips carry exactly one).
An utterance whose prefix could stand as a finished request is NOT admitted as an 'incomplete' cut; ambiguous cuts are rejected at review, never labelled by majority.

rejection_classes_humdial.source: HumDial Track-2 (ICASSP 2026 challenge) class names; the definitions below are OURS, one line each, and the mapping is nearest-equivalent, never identical to the organisers' annotation.

URB.name: user real-time backchannel
URB.definition: Acknowledgement speech while the assistant is talking that must not interrupt it.

PH.name: pause handling
PH.definition: A mid-utterance pause after which the user continues, so the system must stay silent through it.

TPS.name: third-party speech
TPS.definition: Speech from someone other than the user (a bystander) that must not trigger a response or an interruption.

SDO.name: speech directed at others
SDO.definition: The user talking to another person in the room, not to the assistant.

interruption_classes_humdial.source: HumDial Track-2 class names; definitions are ours.

FQ.name: follow-up question
FQ.definition: The user cuts in with a question that builds on what the assistant was saying; the assistant should stop and answer.

ND.name: negation / dissatisfaction
ND.definition: The user cuts in to reject, correct or complain about what was said; the assistant should stop and repair.

RR.name: repetition request
RR.definition: The user cuts in asking the assistant to repeat or restate; the assistant should stop and repeat.

TS.name: topic switch
TS.definition: The user cuts in to change the subject; the assistant should stop and follow the new topic.

ST.name: silence / termination
ST.definition: The user cuts in to stop the assistant ('stop', 'be quiet'); the assistant should stop and not resume on its own.

badcat_style_interrupt_classes.source: Badcat full-duplex submission prompt (explicit rebuttal / negation, question, request to stop or correct => interrupt; agreement / response / encouragement => continue). Our own one-line definitions.
badcat_style_interrupt_classes.interrupt_explicit_rebuttal: User contradicts or negates the assistant ('that's not right').
badcat_style_interrupt_classes.interrupt_stop: User tells the assistant to stop, wait or correct itself ('stop', 'hold on, that is wrong').
badcat_style_interrupt_classes.continue_acknowledgement: User agrees, acknowledges or encourages ('yeah', 'got it', 'good point'); the assistant keeps talking. Equivalent to the turn state 'backchannel'.

overlap_classes.talking_to_others: Speech by the enrolled user that is addressed to a third person; must not trigger a reply and must not cancel assistant output (HumDial SDO).
overlap_classes.background_speech: Speech by non-enrolled people, a TV or a radio at conversational level; must not trigger a reply and must not cancel assistant output (HumDial TPS).
overlap_classes.annotation_status: classes are defined here and consumed by CS-48 overlap stimuli; the synthesized CS-45 stratum contains no talking_to_others / background_speech clips (those need real room acoustics and a second voice mixed at level); FDB v1.5 data and the human-recorded stratum supply them when fetched or recorded.

self_correction.definition: Mid-utterance change of intent by the same speaker ('set a timer for ten, no, fifteen minutes'); the later content supersedes the earlier.
self_correction.turn_state: incomplete until the corrected content is complete, then complete.
self_correction.scoring: NOT scored by CS-45/CS-47. Tool-call correctness after a self-correction is left to CS-24 / CS-36; CS-45 only freezes the field so recordings made now carry it.
self_correction.synthesized_coverage: none (class annotated now for human recordings; no synthesized clips carry it)

CUT_IC.definition: One rendered recording; member a runs to its natural end, member b is cut at a word boundary inside a clause, then both get exactly 2.0 s of digital silence.

CUT_WAIT.definition: One rendered recording of a hold request plus a content-changing continuation; member b is cut after the hold request, member a runs on.

CTX_BC.definition: One rendered acknowledgement waveform (sample-identical in both members); a = placed after the assistant finished a question, b = placed over an assistant monologue that keeps going.

pair_construction_invariants: identical waveform: the user channel is sample-identical over the shared span (cut pairs: from the onset to the shorter segment minus the 10 ms fade; context pairs: the whole faded segment)
matched trailing silence: exactly 32000 samples (2.0 s) of digital zero on the user channel after the user segment, in both members; the clip ends there
cut pairs carry identical assistant context; context pairs differ ONLY in the assistant channel and in the clock position of the user segment
both members of a pair share speaker, dialogue, split and stratum

strata.synthesized: qwentts.cpp production kernel, voices cloned from LibriSpeech speaker embeddings; may reject or rank an arm, never advance one
strata.human_recorded: real human speech (CS-4 sets 2 and 5, operator recordings, public sets where the licence allows); the ONLY stratum on which an arm can advance

mapping_to_turnbench.complete: an 'eot' prediction inside [eot_gold_s - 0.25, eot_gold_s + 3.0] s is a true positive with signed latency t_pred - eot_gold_s (TurnBench window)
mapping_to_turnbench.incomplete_wait: mid-turn-pause negative span; an 'eot' prediction inside it is a false positive (at most one per span)
mapping_to_turnbench.backchannel: backchannel negative; an 'interruption' prediction on the user channel inside the span is the INT false positive (at most one per span); an end-of-turn / yield decision there is additionally a false yield in the paired yield/keep PASR rows of CS-47
